q: In which kind of graph does BFS give the shortest path in terms of the number of edges?
expl: BFS explores layer by layer, so the first time it reaches a vertex is via the fewest edges - true whenever all edges count equally (unweighted).

q: Which data structure does breadth-first search use?
expl: BFS keeps a FIFO queue of discovered vertices. DFS uses a stack (explicitly or via recursion).

q: What is true about the adjacency matrix of an undirected graph?
opts: It is always a diagonal matrix
expl: An undirected edge i-j sets BOTH adj[i][j] and adj[j][i] to 1, so the matrix mirrors across its diagonal (that is why addEdge sets both).

q: Which approach produces a topological ordering of a DAG?
opts: Repeatedly removing a vertex with in-degree zero
Repeatedly removing the vertex of maximum degree
Visiting edges in decreasing order of weight
ansText: Repeatedly removing a vertex with in-degree zero
expl: Kahn's algorithm: take any vertex with no incoming edges left, output it, delete its outgoing edges, repeat. This is also the basis of the 'minimum semesters' program.

q: Which data structure does an iterative depth first search use?
expl: DFS goes deep first and backtracks - exactly LIFO behaviour (recursion uses the call stack automatically).

q: What is the space complexity of the adjacency matrix representation of a graph with V vertices?
expl: A V x V matrix stores V² cells whether or not edges exist - fine for small V (like the 15-vertex problems here), wasteful for large sparse graphs.

q: A topological ordering exists only for which kind of graph?
expl: A cycle means every vertex in it always has an in-degree > 0, so no valid order exists - the 'Impossible: Cycle in prerequisites' output.

q: What is the space complexity of the adjacency list representation of a graph with V vertices and E edges?
expl: One list per vertex plus one entry per edge - much better than O(V²) when the graph is sparse (few edges).

q: Dijkstra's algorithm does not give correct results for graphs containing which kind of edges?
expl: Dijkstra marks a vertex 'done' too early, so a later negative edge can no longer improve it - use Bellman-Ford when negative edges exist.

q: How does Prim's algorithm grow a minimum spanning tree?
opts: By adding the heaviest edge that connects the tree to a new vertex
By adding the minimum-weight edge that connects the tree to a new vertex
By visiting vertices in depth first order
ansText: By adding the minimum-weight edge that connects the tree to a new vertex
expl: At every step Prim takes the cheapest edge crossing from the tree built so far to an outside vertex (key[v] update in the MST program).

q: When is an undirected graph said to be connected?
opts: There is a path between every pair of vertices
ansText: There is a path between every pair of vertices
expl: All vertices must be in one component. The components program counts groups by running DFS from every unvisited vertex.

q: How many edges does a minimum spanning tree of a connected graph with V vertices have?
expl: A spanning tree connects all V vertices with exactly V - 1 edges - any more would create a cycle.

q: Which of the following is a real-world application of graphs?
opts: Modelling road networks and social networks
ansText: Modelling road networks and social networks
expl: Anything made of nodes + connections (roads, friendships, metro lines, prerequisites) is naturally a graph.

expl: Bellman-Ford relaxes all edges V-1 times and then runs one extra pass: if anything still improves, a negative cycle exists (used in the courier-cost program).
